payload.headline: Microsoft falls 2.77% to 484.52, breaking support; hold, add nearer 475.73

summary.thesis: The business keeps getting better, but free cash flow fell from 78.0B to 60.0B, so the price only makes sense if heavy spending starts paying back.
summary.decision: Hold. Add only near the low end of the stock's usual valuation range, and leave the swing trade alone until price picks a side.

payload.happening: Microsoft fell 2.77% to 484.52. It closed below the 486.0–491.22 zone, which had 8 touches and was yesterday's add level. That zone now sits overhead as resistance, a price area where selling has capped rallies. There is no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: Today's drop is about price, not the business. There is no news, so nothing about demand, margins or competition changed today. The latest filed quarter is still solid. Sales grew 18.8% from a year earlier, up from 18.3% two quarters ago. The operating margin (the share of sales left after running costs) rose to 47.1% from 46.27%. The balance sheet has 29.0B more cash than debt, and the share count shrank 0.27%. Analysts keep raising their numbers. The next-year earnings-per-share estimate rose to 24.2 from 23.68 thirty days ago. Cash is the weak spot. Free cash flow, the cash left after investment, fell to 60.0B from 78.0B, and only 17.31% of sales turns into free cash. The filings say each dollar invested now earns 30¢ a year, down from 51¢ three years ago. The spending is real, but it is not paying back yet (general knowledge: much of it is reported to be AI data-center build-out). Earnings power is not at risk. The risk is that cash returns on that spending stay low for longer than the price assumes.

worth.text: The price is 25.3 times trailing earnings and 20.0 times next year's estimate. It is also 10.4 times sales, against a peer median of 3.5. A discounted cash flow model values a business on its future cash, discounted back to today. Starting from today's 60.0B of free cash flow, it gives 180.1 to 286.88 per share, with a base of 217.44. To justify the current price, free cash flow would have to start growing at about 39.7% a year. Even 30% starting growth only gets to 341.8. Against its own past, the picture is different. Using its usual 5-year price-to-sales range, the stock is worth 475.73 to 592.92, with a middle of 535.43. Today's price-to-sales sits at the 33rd percentile of its own 5-year history. The two methods are more than 2x apart, and one assumption explains the gap. The cash-flow model takes today's depressed cash flow as the starting point. The history method assumes investors keep paying what they have paid before. Two of three measures lean expensive. Because the business is improving, the fair range uses the own-history numbers, and the price now sits near the bottom of that range.
worth.key_assumption: The spending that cut free cash flow from 78.0B to 60.0B turns back into cash, so next-year earnings (estimate 24.2) are the right basis for value, not today's cash flow.

bull: Growth is speeding up, not slowing: quarterly sales growth was 18.8% versus 18.3% two quarters ago.
Profitability is still rising: operating margin is 47.1%, up from 46.27%.
Analysts are raising forecasts: the next-year EPS estimate is 24.2, up from 23.68 thirty days ago, and the price is 20.0 times that figure.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 60.0B from 78.0B, and each invested dollar now earns 30¢ versus 51¢ three years ago.
The cash-flow base value is 217.44, and today's price needs free cash flow to start growing at about 39.7% a year.
The stock costs 10.4 times sales against a peer median of 3.5, which leaves little room for a miss.

levels.what: Today's close is just above the 475.73 low of the own-history range. Nothing here calls for selling, but the stock just broke a level, so this is not the spot to add.
Bottom of the own-history fair range, inside the 472.2–480.69 support zone (3 touches). Add here.
Bottom of the lower support zone (461.96–467.91, 4 touches). A close below it would put the price under both support zones and under the fair range, so hold off on adding until the 2027-01-27 report.

longterm.why: The business is improving and estimates are rising, but cash flow is weak and two of three valuation measures lean expensive. Today's break moved the add level down from 491.22 to 475.73.

swing.why: Price fell below the 486.0–491.22 zone and is under the falling 20-day average (522.04) and the flat 50-day average (519.39). The next support, 472.2–480.69, sits just below, so there is little room either way relative to the 16.39 average daily range. The setup becomes valid only on a close back above 491.22: entry 491.22, stop 480.69, target 503.99.

decision.timing: The 2027-02-19 options price a 13.7% move and cover the 2027-01-27 report, so new long-term money beyond the 475.73 add waits for that report's free cash flow figure.

change_mind: A close below 461.96, the bottom of both support zones, would change the long-term action from hold to wait until the 2027-01-27 report.
In the 2027-01-27 report, trailing free cash flow rising back above 60.0B would support moving to add, and a further fall would support trimming.
The next-year EPS estimate falling back below 23.68 would mean the analyst upgrades that support the hold are reversing.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still a hold; the close at 484.52, below the 486.0–491.22 zone, confirmed it and moved the add level down from 491.22 to 475.73.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
